newsitem.title: USA: Merrill Lynch to change muni procedures nationwide.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch to change muni procedures nationwide.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co will adopt municipal bond procedural and training changes nationwide, expanding voluntarily on its pact with the Orange County district attorney, a spokesman said Friday.
On Thursday, Merrill Lynch agreed to pay $30 million to settle a 2-1/2-year investigation by the Orange County district attorney into the county's 1994 bankruptcy debacle.
Under the settlement, Merrill Lynch also agreed to implement procedural and training changes in California.
Merrill Lynch spokesman Timothy Gilles said Friday the brokerage firm would make the changes across the country.
"We believe that our prior procedures were adequate," Gilles said. But he added: "The (new) procedures have merit and we intend to implement them nationwide."
"It will ensure that offerings that Merrill Lynch underwrites will continue to meet the highest standards," Gilles said.

Merrill Lynch's settlement marked the end of the Orange County district attorney's probe of the powerful New York brokerage firm and other Wall Street bond houses, and ensured Merrill Lynch and its employees will not face criminal charges.
Merrill Lynch, which has denied any wrongdoing, said it agreed to the out-of-court settlement to avoid the "cost and distraction" of litigation.
In addition to paying $30 million, Merrill Lynch agreed to change the way it trains employees and improve the way information about a municipal bond issuer is gathered, coordinated and disclosed.

Under the settlement, Merrill Lynch would designate a "disclosure agent" for each deal. The agent would coordinate with various company departments to "elicit any material information in their possession about the issuer."

Orange County shocked Wall Street in December 1994 when it filed for bankruptcy after losing more than $1.6 billion on risky investments made by its once-respected treasurer, Robert Citron. The county emerged from bankruptcy one year ago.
For 2-1/2 years county prosecutors have been investigating bond firms, including Merrill Lynch, and other financial professionals in connection with the crisis.

Merrill Lynch approached the district attorney's office several weeks ago to initiate settlement talks, according to county prosecutors. At the time, prosecutors were considering the filing of a civil complaint against Merrill Lynch for unfair business practices and false advertising.
